paper.title: AccelOpt: A Self-Improving LLM Agentic System for AI Accelerator Kernel Optimization
paper.central_claim: AccelOpt, a self-improving LLM agentic system combining beam search with an optimization memory of slow-fast kernel pairs, autonomously optimizes AWS Trainium NKI kernels without expert optimization knowledge, raising average percent-of-peak 49->61% (Trn1) and 45->59% (Trn2) and matching Claude Sonnet 4 at 26x lower cost.

rationale: 束搜索加按问题的慢快核对记忆，在14个自建内核上提速；记忆主要省成本而非提高最优值，无重复运行，选择集即报告集。

sections_read: Appendix A (A.1 extra, A.2 experiment details, A.3 prompts, tables)

evidence.quote: AccelOpt explores the kernel optimization space through iterative generation, informed by an optimization memory that curates experiences and insights from previously encountered slow-fast kernel pairs.
evidence.support_explanation: States the retained non-weight component: a curated optimization memory built from measured slow-fast kernel pairs.

evidence.quote: However, it does not significantly improve the performance of the best kernels discovered if enough kernels are sampled, compared to beam search alone.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' own finding: memory does not raise the best discovered speedup once enough kernels are sampled; its measured value is cost-efficiency.

evidence.quote: the optimization memory is maintained as a queue of optimization items with a capacity cap (ExpN)
evidence.support_explanation: Memory is a bounded FIFO queue (ExpN=16 in main runs).

evidence.quote: Each new iteration can append up to TopK experience items to the tail, while the oldest entries in the memory will be discarded once ExpN is reached.
evidence.support_explanation: Write/forget rule: append TopK new items, evict oldest; eviction is by age, not by measured utility.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.4 Optimization Memory vs. Beam Search Only
evidence.quote: search-only experiments run the total T=16 iterations, while Search + Memory experiments achieve similar speedup in 13 iterations, saving 16-17% cost.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory ablation result: similar best speedup in 13 vs 16 iterations (16-17% cost saving); curves only in Figs 13-14.

evidence.quote: Reflexion-style baseline achieves 1.137 × \times speedup ($178.37) versus 1.235 × \times ($139.00) for AccelOpt.
evidence.support_explanation: Matched kernel-count comparison (144 trajectories x T=16) against a Reflexion-style reflector: 1.137x vs 1.235x geomean speedup, and higher cost for the baseline.

evidence.quote: B=1 with memory achieves final best speedup 1.204 × \times ($143.58), and B=1 without memory achieves 1.229 × \times ($116.35).
evidence.support_explanation: With a single beam candidate, memory is worse than no memory (1.204 vs 1.229), i.e. memory can hurt when candidates lack diversity.

evidence.quote: Qwen3-Coder-30B gains 4.6% speedup improvement with extra $12.33 cost. On the contrary, the extra $13.81 cost only brings 0.6% speedup improvement in gpt-oss-120b.
evidence.support_explanation: Doubling memory capacity from ExpN=8 to 16: +4.6% for one executor model but +0.6% for gpt-oss-120b (1.228->1.235), differences at noise level without repeats.

evidence.quote: Claude Sonnet 4 Claude Sonnet 4 1.226 ($1732.73) gpt-oss-120b Claude Sonnet 4 1.213 ($1269.98) Claude Sonnet 4 gpt-oss-120b 1.208 ($1223.05) gpt-oss-120b gpt-oss-120b 1.235 ($139.00)
evidence.support_explanation: AccelOpt with Claude Sonnet 4 reaches 1.226 at $1733; the open-source configuration reaches 1.235 at $139, so the cost advantage comes from the model choice, not the memory.

evidence.quote: repeated sampling speedup 1.222 × \times ($5806.83)
evidence.support_explanation: Claude Sonnet 4 repeated-sampling baseline: 1.222x at $5806.83 (no beam search, no memory).

evidence.quote: can exploit the correctness checker for certain kernel workloads. For example, it proposes to compute only the row-wise maximum of the first tile in each row chunk to achieve fake speedup by omitting necessary computation in safe softamx.
evidence.support_explanation: Verifier weakness: the correctness check (random-input comparison with CPU reference) can be gamed; authors do not state that reported best kernels were audited for equivalence.

evidence.quote: we use B=6 and K=12 for other experiments
evidence.support_explanation: Search hyperparameters were chosen from comparisons on the same NKIBench tasks later used for reporting; no separate tuning split.

evidence.quote: that applies on a per-problem basis for iterative kernel optimization, where optimization insights transfer from previous iterations to future ones
evidence.support_explanation: Memory scope is per problem; later iterations of the same problem are the only consumers.

evidence.quote: Studying how to transfer the memory accumulated from optimizing some kernels to others is worth future exploration.
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-kernel transfer of the memory is explicitly untested.

evidence.quote: To further mitigate fluctuation, we conduct several rounds and select the one with the smallest relative difference, or the first within a predefined threshold.
evidence.support_explanation: Latency measurement protocol includes warm-up and repeated rounds; reduces timing noise; selection of the 'smallest-difference round' is a protocol choice.

evidence.quote: AccelOpt with gpt-oss-120b achieved 1.27 × 1.27\times average speedup over best Triton baselines
evidence.support_explanation: Out-of-NKIBench check on 24 H100 Triton kernels (FlashInfer-Bench) with platform-specific prompts; results only in Appendix Fig 18.

evidence.quote: AccelOpt cannot do effective exploration because the initial kernel is challenging to optimize
evidence.support_explanation: Authors report a saturation failure mode without effective exploration (small-K Matmul-like kernels).

evidence.quote: AccelOpt improves the average throughput from 49 % 49\% to 61 % 61\% of peak on Trainium 1 and from 45 % 45\% to 59 % 59\% on Trainium 2
evidence.support_explanation: Headline: average percentage of peak over 14 NKIBench kernels; this is task-level improvement of the discovered kernels, not a held-out measure of learned memory.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.4 Beam Search vs. Repeated Sampling Only
evidence.quote: beam search outperforms repeated sampling of the agentic workflow, using the same LLMs
evidence.support_explanation: Beam-search accumulation (not memory) is the main driver of progress; shown in Figs 12-13.

evidence.quote: It is thus difficult to set up a fair comparison with these methods.
evidence.support_explanation: No non-LLM autotuner baseline is run.

evidence.quote: allowing the system to dynamically allocate more sampling budget to difficult cases where no improvement was achieved.
evidence.support_explanation: Candidate-selection rule falls back to previous candidates when no improvement is found; an evaluation-allocation mechanism.

evidence.quote: This guide is adopted from the public NKI programming document and tuned for the agents based on their common errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Agents are given human-written NKI API/hardware constraints tuned on observed agent errors; 'no expert knowledge' applies to optimization recipes, not to API/hardware facts.

signatures.object: Per-problem optimization memory: queue of experience items (slow-fast kernel pair pseudo-code + LLM-written general strategy) read by the planner
signatures.information: Measured latency and profile of generated kernels, correctness against CPU reference; planner sees current candidate, profile and memory; summarizer sees selected slow/fast pairs
signatures.operation: Group generated kernels by (candidate, plan); pair outliers above t_pos=1.04 (positive) or below 1/t_neg (negative rewrites); summarizer writes strategy; append TopK=8, cap ExpN=16, drop oldest
signatures.output: Updated memory E_i used in the next iteration's planner prompt
signatures.conditions: Needs a profiler giving reliable latency; candidates should be diverse (B=1 case, E007); executor model must be capable (E008)
signatures.feedback: Hardware profile/latency and correctness result per generated kernel
signatures.selection_rule: Speedup thresholds + top-K by sorted speedup within subgroups; FIFO eviction
signatures.selection_data: Same problem's measured latency (selection set = reporting set)
signatures.persistence: In-run memory for one kernel optimization campaign; not shared across problems (E013, E014)
signatures.later_use: Planner conditions every later iteration on the whole queue
signatures.claimed_effect: Similar best speedup in 13 vs 16 iterations (16-17% cost saving), higher cumulative Fast@p; authors also say best-kernel speedup is not significantly improved (E002)
signatures.failure_boundary: Hurts with a single candidate (1.204 vs 1.229); ExpN effect model-dependent; no cross-problem transfer

signatures.object: Candidate-kernel frontier (beam) and the planner/executor workflow that generates new kernels
signatures.operation: Planner samples N plans per candidate, executor implements each K times, profiler scores B*N*K kernels, beta keeps best-correct per plan group then top-B by latency, fills from previous candidates
signatures.conditions: Correctness tolerance per task, per-task distributed profiling
signatures.selection_rule: Fastest correct per plan group, then top-B
signatures.selection_data: Measured latency on the benchmark inputs
signatures.persistence: Beam candidates for the run; best kernel is the deliverable
signatures.claimed_effect: Beam search outperforms repeated sampling with the same LLMs (E019); average peak fraction 49->61 / 45->59 (E018)
signatures.failure_boundary: Saturation near peak or with hard initial kernels (E017); checker exploitation (E011)

gap.author_gap: New accelerators (Trainium/NKI) lack expert optimization recipes; exploring a huge kernel design space with LLM queries is costly; existing LLM kernel systems need hand-crafted optimization lists or are closed.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and concrete (relative to Autocomp's manually crafted problem-specific lists and GEPA's prompt evolution), but the asserted residual that experience accumulation closes it is only weakly supported: the paper's own results show beam search drives the gains and memory mainly saves cost (E002, E019).
gap.lineage: Test-time scaling by repeated sampling -> beam search over LLM kernels (Autocomp) -> evolving memory/reflection (Reflexion, LessonL baseline-anchored) -> AccelOpt: beam search + curated slow-fast pair memory with positive and negative items.
gap.closest_adjacent: Autocomp (beam search, hand-written optimization lists), AlphaEvolve (closed), GEPA (evolves prompts for NPU kernels), LessonL (CPU, baseline-anchored memory), Reflexion-style reflector (re-implemented as baseline, E006).
gap.residue: Memory transfer across kernels; verifier robustness; whether FIFO text memory is the right store; cost of profiling hardware.
gap.stakes: Per-kernel LLM cost at thousands-of-kernels scale; autonomy on new hardware.
gap.method_response: Beam search for cumulative gains + memory of measured slow-fast pairs injected into the planner; open-source models for cost.
gap.remaining_gap: Per-problem scope only (E013-14), no item-level utility credit or retirement, small best-speedup effect of memory, exploitable checker.
gap.unresolved: Autocomp/GEPA/LessonL source texts not fixed locally; their comparison is taken from this paper's related-work paragraph.

rs_pattern.reason: Kernel generation is split into planner / executor / summarizer roles, and the generated artifact is executable code that a sound external checker and hardware profiler score; that verifiable signal selects candidates and curates the reusable memory. The planner->executor handoff is natural-language, not a typed artifact, so fit is partial.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Step1 responsibility boundary: roles are LLM prompts; the sound component is the profiler/CPU-reference checker. Step2 machine-checkable artifact: kernel code is executable and checked; plan text is advisory. Step3 loop closed on verifiable output used in selection and memory credit: yes. Step4 ablate verification feedback: not done as such (beam search and memory ablated instead). Step5 cost reported: yes ($).
matches.success_checks: By-products accumulated as reusable capital (memory): yes, per problem. Obtainable signals only (profile, latency): yes. Single load-bearing mechanism isolated: partly (beam search vs memory).
matches.failure_checks: Assembly of off-the-shelf agents: partially present (generic planner/executor/summarizer prompts). Unmeasured solver cost: avoided. Self-improvement loop with unvalidated intermediates: summarizer outputs are not independently validated.
matches.reason: Operation executed is the profiler-closed generate-score-select loop; domain framing (kernels) adds no separate RS card.

matches.condition_checks: step1 checkable unit: partial (pseudo-code pair + strategy, not re-tested individually); step2 credit by evidence: partial (pair speedup thresholds relative to originating candidate, negative items kept, no repeated-observation gating); step3 bound/structure: partial (cap + FIFO, no hierarchy/backtrack); step4 declare/test sharing scope: unmet (per problem, transfer deferred); step5 matched-budget memory ablation with held-out: partial (Search vs Search+Memory, iteration-matched not token-matched; no held-out).

evaluator-first: met (profiling service, CPU reference); evolved unit small in scaffold: unmet (whole kernels); grounded mutations in evaluator traces: met (profile in planner prompt); deliberate evaluation spending: partial (beta allocation, fallback to prior candidates; no novelty filter); selection/reporting separation and variance: unmet.

revision_proposals: H15 could add an explicit sub-condition for per-problem (non-transferred) memory scope with iteration-count rather than token-matched ablation.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS C25: verifiable solver output closes the loop and by-products become reusable capital. Domain H15: measured fitness deltas credit a knowledge layer that conditions later proposals.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_or_differences: RS has no population/archive notion; domain H14/H15 require held-out separation and item-level credit, which the paper lacks.

claims.text: AccelOpt with open-source models raises average percentage of peak throughput from 49% to 61% (Trn1) and 45% to 59% (Trn2) on NKIBench.
claims.baseline_control: initial NKIBench kernels (mostly Neuron compiler output)
claims.selection_vs_test: same kernels and inputs for selection and reporting
claims.result_denominator: 14 tasks, average of percent-of-peak; per-task figures only as plots
claims.allowed_conclusion: The search procedure finds faster kernels than the starting ones on these 14 tasks, according to the authors' profiler.

claims.text: AccelOpt matches Claude Sonnet 4 repeated sampling at 26x lower cost.
claims.setting: gpt-oss-120b planner/summarizer, Qwen3-Coder-480B executor; Claude with thinking, repeated sampling
claims.baseline_control: Claude Sonnet 4 without beam search or memory
claims.result_denominator: geomean over tasks; cost = tokens x list price (Claude reasoning tokens unavailable)
claims.counterevidence: AccelOpt with Claude gives 1.226 at $1733: the cost advantage comes from the model, not the self-improving part
claims.allowed_conclusion: Open-source beam-search agents reach similar geomean speedup at far lower API cost than repeated Claude sampling.

claims.text: The optimization memory makes the system self-improving and cost-effective.
claims.result_denominator: geomean best speedup over 14 tasks; 13 vs 16 iterations
claims.counterevidence: no significant best-speedup gain; B=1 case worse; effects of 0.6-1.7% within unestimated noise
claims.allowed_conclusion: Memory yields a modest iteration/cost saving per problem and beats a re-implemented Reflexion baseline at matched kernel count; it does not demonstrably raise the best speedup.

claims.text: Beam search is more effective than repeated sampling.
claims.baseline_control: repeated sampling of the agentic workflow

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A beam-search planner/executor agent driven by hardware profile feedback finds Trainium kernels with higher percent-of-peak than the starting kernels; a per-problem FIFO memory of slow-fast pairs reduces iterations/cost modestly and beat a Reflexion-style baseline at matched kernel counts, without a demonstrated gain in best speedup.
assessment.cannot_say: That memory causes a retained, transferable improvement; that gains hold on held-out kernels; that reported speedups are free of checker exploitation; effects below a few percent between configurations.
assessment.unresolved: Per-task numbers are in figures only; equivalence audit of the final kernels; hardware cost.
assessment.reproduction_note: All results are author-reported; nothing re-run by us.

G.reason: Real, sourced problem (no expert recipes on a new accelerator, high LLM cost) with explicit neighbours (Autocomp, AlphaEvolve, GEPA, LessonL, Reflexion) and a stated remaining gap (cross-kernel transfer). Not 4: neighbour texts not fixed locally and the proposed residual (memory accumulation) is not shown to be the binding one.

M.reason: Operations, information (profile, slow-fast pairs) and reasons (positive and negative pairs, diversity grouping, FIFO cap) are reconstructible, and the paper produces distinguishing observations (memory hurts at B=1, planner choice irrelevant while executor matters, Reflexion reflecting on all kernels costs more). Weak: heuristic thresholds, unvalidated summarizer, memory shown not to raise best speedup.

X.reason: Memory write/selection/eviction and next-iteration read are fully specified with hyperparameters; failure and saturation analysis plus platform requirements are given. No item-level utility check, versioning, rollback or conflict handling; scope limited to one problem.

E.measurement.reason: Latency with warm-up and repeated rounds, roofline-based percent-of-peak, multi-seed tolerance checks give a credible metric, but the authors document that the checker can be exploited and do not state an equivalence audit of reported kernels; no non-LLM baseline.

E.causality.reason: Useful controls (beam vs repeated sampling, memory vs none, B=1, TopK/ExpN sweeps, Reflexion-style baseline at matched kernels, models swapped) but memory effect is small and mostly figure-only, no per-role ablation, no repeats; cost advantage vs Claude is due to model choice.

E.holdout.reason: Selection (best measured latency), hyperparameter choice and reporting all use the same 14 kernels; memory is used only on the same problem; anecdotal out-of-benchmark results (Conv2D course, 24 Triton kernels) exist but are not controlled.

E.statistics.reason: No repeated runs, seeds or intervals; differences of 0.6-4.6% are interpreted; per-task plots and saturation failure cases are shown (credit), but no run-to-run variance.

E.cost.reason: Dollar costs for nearly every configuration, cost-benefit sweeps and baselines at matched generated-kernel counts; Claude reasoning tokens not countable (conservative); profiling hardware time and failed-kernel profiling excluded; iteration-matched rather than token-matched memory ablation.
